summary.en: Bank accounts are registered as "resident" or "non-resident" under the Foreign Exchange Act. This is separate from your residence status and from tax residency, and it is not decided by nationality or months in Japan alone. According to bank guidance, a person without Japanese nationality is a resident after 6 months from entry, or when working at an office in Japan. Japanese nationals who lived abroad may be non-residents. Your bank's registration may not match your current situation. Telling the bank is not a legal deadline. Fees and transfer rules differ by bank. First ask your bank how you are registered (to be checked).

lead.en: Ask your bank whether you are registered as a "resident" or a "non-resident".

text.en: If you do not have Japanese nationality: you are a non-resident if less than 6 months have passed since you entered Japan and you do not work at an office in Japan (Japan Post Bank guidance). Even before 6 months, you are a resident if you work at an office in Japan. Some banks do not count part-time jobs for this (example: MUFG Bank; to be checked). The 6 months count from the day you entered Japan, not from the day you registered your address. Foreign government officials and diplomats are treated differently.

text.en: Japanese nationals are usually residents. However, you are a non-resident if you left Japan to work at an office abroad, left intending to stay abroad for 2 years or more, or have stayed abroad for 2 years or more since leaving. A temporary visit to Japan of less than 6 months (for example on holiday) does not change this (Japan Post Bank guidance). When you come back to live in Japan, ask your bank about your registration (to be checked).
